extracted.intended_audience: applicants and institutional staff preparing NIH grant application components (Facilities & Other Resources, Senior/Key Person Profile, Biographical Sketch) and reviewers assessing resource/compliance elements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required content for the 'Facilities & Other Resources' section, equipment/core access, animal-use compliance, and the Senior/Key Person Profile / Biographical Sketch portions of an NIH grant application. Covers facility designations, training and oversight requirements, core/center resources, voucher eligibility criteria, and required form fields/attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSL-2 laboratory designation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cassat laboratory is designated as a Biohazard Safety Level 2 facility, meaning that all equipment and resources are in place to work with the biohazardous agents described in this application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities must be specifically designed and equipped to support the proposed research (here, at the crossroads of microbiology and bone biology). All members must undergo extensive training prior to working with biohazardous material; the applicant states 'I have completed all the necessary training to work in a Biosafety Level 2 laboratory.'

rubrics_metrics.name: IACUC review and approval required prior to initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposed activities using vertebrate animals at VUMC and VU are reviewed and approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IACUC (and a standing Animal Care Committee) must review and approve all animal research protocols prior to their initialization. The IACUC establishes policies (e.g., acceptable mouse cage density, food/water regulation) and reviews, semi-annually, the animal care program and all animal housing and study areas. The facility is accredited by AAALAC and the U.S. Department of Agriculture; administrative support is provided by the Office of Animal Welfare Association (OAWA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel training and testing for IACUC protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: All personnel listed on IACUC protocols must complete required training modules and pass the corresponding tests contained within each module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has completed Animal Biohazard Safety Level 2 (ABSL-2) training. To remain compliant with any new ABSL-2 or IACUC regulations, the applicant will continue to attend ABSL-2 refresher training courses annually. Training completion and testing are prerequisites for personnel to be listed on protocols and to work with animals/biohazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of designated ABSL-2 animal facility and suite requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals for this study will be procured through and housed in a BSL-2 Animal Facility located in Medical Center North; the lab’s designated animal space in suite A-8223 includes a mouse breeding facility free of infectious agents, housing and procedure rooms, biohazard cabinets, anesthesia machines, euthanasia systems, and sterile food/water/cages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All animal procedures and harvests will be conducted in the designated suite to ensure safety and sterility. An online reservation system for biosafety cabinets confirms equipment availability when necessary. ABSL-2 facilities are critical for conducting infections and dissections with sterility and safety in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal husbandry, veterinary care, and record-keeping standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Animal Care provides procurement, husbandry and veterinary care services including a comprehensive preventative medicine and veterinary care program with daily observation by animal care, veterinary, and research staffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animals identified as ill or injured receive veterinary examination and treatment as deemed appropriate; veterinarians/veterinary technicians communicate directly with investigative staff and treatments are documented and 'closed out' upon resolution. Records are maintained by the animal’s individual record-keeper. Proper husbandry and veterinary oversight are described as 'critical' to research success.

rubrics_metrics.name: VICTR Voucher and Pilot Program eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: VICTR provides a Voucher and Pilot Program offering awards for preliminary data and pilot work; submitted projects are required to meet specified criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility/acceptance criteria (verbatim): 'clinical and translational research, meaning it involves human subjects, human tissue, human cell lines, and/or human information; hypothesis driven with specific research question; and appropriately powered to obtain preliminary data.' Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and all researchers are eligible to apply. Vouchers may be used to bridge mouse-model discoveries into human cells/samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and core support for imaging (VUIIS / CSAI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Center for Small Animal Imaging (CSAI) provides training for users on optical imaging and expert support/training for data/image analysis; VUIIS offers state-of-the-art small animal imaging modalities and instrumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators must receive appropriate training to use imaging equipment (example: applicant trained on Scanco microCT50 with training and assistance provided by a named faculty member). Support and expertise from VUIIS faculty are cited as essential for development of analysis programs and precise quantification in imaging-based studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to VCBB instrumentation and expert co-sponsorship
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vanderbilt Center for Bone Biology (VCBB) provides multiple high-tech instruments for molecular, cellular, biochemical, histology and bone morphometry studies and offers technical support, training, and a weekly seminar series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a primary faculty member of VCBB confers access and training on specialized instrumentation. Co-sponsorship (e.g., by VCBB faculty) and access to core experts (bone histology core head) facilitate acquisition of new skills and technical support necessary to complete proposed studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & equipment availability as evidence of project feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to equipment within the laboratory, VUIIS, and VCBB demonstrates readiness to perform the methods required by the research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application enumerates specific laboratory instruments (e.g., centrifuges, biosafety cabinets, microscopes, incubators, microplate reader, gel documentation, -80°C freezer, microCT scanners, MRI/PET/SPECT systems, histology microtomes, BIOQUANT/OsteoMeasure software). A complete equipment inventory and core access are presented to support the claim that the investigator is 'uniquely positioned' to conduct the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Person Profile required fields and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) requires specific identity, role, and document attachments for senior/key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required form elements shown include: Prefix, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Position/Title, Organization Name, Department/Division, Street/City/State/Country/Zip, Phone Number, E-Mail, Project Role (e.g., PD/PI), Degree Type, Degree Year, Attach Biographical Sketch (file name), Attach Current & Pending Support (file name), and Tracking Number. Funding Opportunity Number and Received Date are also recorded. Attachments (biosketch, current & pending support) must be provided with file names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Biographical Sketch structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Biographical Sketch is organized into labeled sections (A. Personal Statement; B. Positions and Honors; C. Contributions to Science) and includes education/training, personal statement, positions, honors, publications/abstracts, and contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal Statement should summarize research goals and relevance to the proposed project. Positions and Honors must list activities and dates. Contributions to Science should describe major areas of contribution with supporting citations (publications, abstracts, presentations). Education/training table must include institution, degree, start/end dates, and field of study. Lists of students trained, awards, and society memberships provide supporting evidence of qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete equipment inventory for cores/shared space
rubrics_metrics.description: Shared laboratory spaces and cores (VCBB, VUIIS, Cassat lab) must list available general, molecular, imaging, and histology equipment to demonstrate capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document provides explicit inventories (e.g., specific models of MRI, microCT scanners, microplate readers, qPCR instruments, microtomes, imaging systems, centrifuges, incubators, freezers, analysis software such as FIJI, GraphPad Prism, ReadCube, BIOQUANT, OsteoMeasure). A clear, detailed inventory supports reviewers' assessment of resource adequacy and feasibility.
